more: KB versus kB

Strictly, 1 kB is 1,000 bytes and 1 KiB is 1,024 bytes, but most websites and operating systems call 1,024 bytes a KB. The default uses 1,024, so a 50 KB target means at most 51,200 bytes. If a form rejects the file by a whisker, switch the unit or enter a slightly lower target.
Quality first, then size

Lowering JPEG quality removes fine detail that the eye barely notices, while shrinking dimensions makes everything smaller. The compressor therefore keeps your original resolution as long as quality stays at an acceptable level and only scales down when necessary, reporting the final quality and dimensions for each image.
Your files stay local

more: Why GIFs are so big

GIF stores each frame using up to 256 colours and compresses only by repeating patterns, with no motion prediction like modern video codecs. Noisy pixels or dithering that change from frame to frame break those patterns. The lossy option replaces pixels that barely changed with the previous frame's colour, creating long identical runs that compress well.

Decoding and encoding happen in your browser, so even GIFs of private screens are never uploaded.

It cuts the sound into short overlapping pieces, then lays them closer together or further apart, choosing the best alignment for each piece so the waveform stays continuous. Pitch shifting combines time-stretching with resampling.

JPEG files are made of segments: EXIF, XMP, IPTC and comments are stored in separate application segments, which this tool drops while copying the image segments as they are. PNG and WEBP use named chunks, and the text, EXIF and XMP chunks are removed in the same way. Other formats are re-encoded as PNG.

more: How it works

The image is scaled to the chosen number of columns, and the brightness of each pixel is mapped to a character from the selected set, from light to dark. The detailed set uses about 70 characters for smooth shading, while the blocks set uses Unicode shading blocks for a pixel-art look.

With colour output each character takes the colour of its pixel, creating a striking HTML file that you can open in any browser. The plain text version is included as a second download.

ascii.name: Image to ASCII Art
ascii.short: Convert pictures to ASCII text art.
ascii.title: Image to ASCII Art Converter – Photo to Text Art Online | {brand}
ascii.desc: Turn any photo or logo into ASCII art with adjustable width, character sets, contrast, invert and colour HTML output. Copy or download as text or HTML. Free and private.
steps: Upload an image.
Adjust width, characters, contrast and colour.
Copy the ASCII art or download it as TXT or HTML.

faq.q: Where can I use ASCII art
faq.a: Plain ASCII art works in code comments, README files, terminal banners, emails in monospaced fonts, forum posts in code blocks and chat apps that support code formatting.

faq.q: Why does it look stretched
faq.a: Characters are about twice as tall as they are wide, so the converter uses half as many rows as columns. View the art in a monospaced font to keep the proportions.
